    • callbackExecutor

      public CheckoutSession.Builder callbackExecutor(Executor callbackExecutor)
      Where asynchronously executed operations deliver their handlers — e.g. an Android main-thread executor so handlers may touch UI directly. Applies to execute(); executeSync() and the blocking accessors are unaffected. Overridable per call with callbackOn(executor). Without one, handlers run directly on the session's operation thread and must be fast, non-blocking, and must never synchronously invoke another session operation.

    • onBackgroundError

      public CheckoutSession.Builder onBackgroundError(Consumer<SessionError> onBackgroundError)
      Handler for failures of work the session performs on its own behalf, with no result object to report through: today the automatic display push after a basket mutation (autoDisplay(boolean)), in the future also the reactive onBasketUpdated(Consumer) channel. Manual updateDisplay(...) failures are not delivered here — they report through their own per-call onError.

      Background failures never interrupt the checkout and are logged whether or not a handler is registered. Delivered through the callbackExecutor when one is configured, directly on the failing thread otherwise.

    • start

      public SessionResult<CheckoutSession> start()
      Validates the configuration and returns a lazy operation that announces the session to the terminal (Nexo Admin session start signal) and yields it once the terminal acknowledged — an unstarted session never exists, so no operation can reach the terminal before the start. Like every session operation, nothing is sent until execute(), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked.

      A refused start yields no session; call start() again for a fresh attempt (each attempt is a new session with a new session ID).

      If the registered onSuccess handler itself throws, the just-started session is ended on the terminal (best-effort) before the exception propagates: a start() whose execution threw never leaves a terminal-side session behind, and any session it may have delivered to the handler must be considered lost.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a required field is missing
